page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-8 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 64 GB of system memory. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7B13 processor with 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The CPU configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the AMD EPYC processor delivers strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% of tested servers. However, multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth—both read and write—fall into the average tier. While single-threaded compression and decompression tasks perform adequately, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is weak, ranking in the bottom 25%. Similarly, LLM inference speeds are average for small 135M models but drop to the bottom 25% for prompt processing on medium 7B models, highlighting a performance tradeoff when scaling to complex multi-threaded or larger language model workloads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2d-highmem-8 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core, making it a resource-dense option for memory-bound workloads without the premium cost of high-end compute or GPU-accelerated hardware. It is well-suited for applications requiring significant memory capacity relative to processing power, such as in-memory databases like Redis, medium-scale web serving, and general-purpose enterprise applications that do not demand intensive multi-threaded parallel processing.
